lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: appointment preparation and questions

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic appointment preparation and questions task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult, the learner identifies one real upcoming appointment, thinks through what information the appointment will likely require and what questions they want answered, writes a complete list, and reviews it with the trusted adult before the appointment happens; the adult confirms the review took place.
safetyNotes: The learner does not attend or conduct the appointment as part of this lesson; only preparation and review with a trusted adult are required.
No real outside party (the appointment provider) is contacted as part of this task; only the learner's own list and a household review are required.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the review by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If the learner has no real upcoming appointment, they instead choose a realistic fictional appointment scenario (such as a first dental visit or a school counselor meeting) and role-play the full preparation and question-review conversation with a trusted adult, with the adult asking follow-up questions the way an appointment provider might, for the same level of review and feedback.

materials: learner-local: paper or a document to write the question list

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one question or piece of information you hadn't thought of before your trusted adult reviewed your list, and why it matters.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Question and information list quality: List includes at least three specific information items and three specific questions relevant to the named appointment type. | Guardian review completion: Guardian confirms the review took place, and the learner names one specific, real detail the adult added or changed. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner prepare a second, shorter version of their list meant for a situation where they only have two minutes to ask their most important question, and explain which question they kept and why.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic appointment preparation and questions task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: paper or a document to write the question list
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: appointment preparation and questions worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult, the learner identifies one real upcoming appointment, thinks through what information the appointment will likely require and what questions they want answered, writes a complete list, and reviews it with the trusted adult before the appointment happens; the adult confirms the review took place.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact appointment preparation and questions decision or action.
Model move 2: Think about a real upcoming appointment you have, or if you don't have one, pick a realistic fictional scenario.
Model move 3: Think through what information you'll likely need to provide and what questions you want to ask.

Model check: Question and information list quality: List includes at least three specific information items and three specific questions relevant to the named appointment type. | Guardian review completion: Guardian confirms the review took place, and the learner names one specific, real detail the adult added or changed.

resources.title: appointment preparation and questions action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for appointment preparation and questions.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: appointment preparation and questions coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult, the learner identifies one real upcoming appointment, thinks through what information the appointment will likely require and what questions they want answered, writes a complete list, and reviews it with the trusted adult before the appointment happens; the adult confirms the review took place.
Coach direction: Think about a real upcoming appointment you have, or if you don't have one, pick a realistic fictional scenario.
Learner prompt: Name the appointment type (real or fictional) and what you already know about what it's for.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: appointment preparation and questions complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Think through what information you'll likely need to provide and what questions you want to ask.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I listed at least three pieces of information I might be asked to provide (such as my age, the reason for the visit, or relevant history).
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wrote at least three specific questions I want answered during the appointment.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Write your full list of information and questions in the order you'd want to bring them up.

Equal-access rule: If the learner has no real upcoming appointment, they instead choose a realistic fictional appointment scenario (such as a first dental visit or a school counselor meeting) and role-play the full preparation and question-review conversation with a trusted adult, with the adult asking follow-up questions the way an appointment provider might, for the same level of review and feedback.

resources.title: appointment preparation and questions minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one question or piece of information you hadn't thought of before your trusted adult reviewed your list, and why it matters.

Success checks: Question and information list quality: List includes at least three specific information items and three specific questions relevant to the named appointment type. | Guardian review completion: Guardian confirms the review took place, and the learner names one specific, real detail the adult added or changed.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: appointment preparation and questions supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional appointment preparation and questions condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Question and information list quality: List includes at least three specific information items and three specific questions relevant to the named appointment type. | Guardian review completion: Guardian confirms the review took place, and the learner names one specific, real detail the adult added or changed..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: With a trusted adult, the learner identifies one real upcoming appointment, thinks through what information the appointment will likely require and what questions they want answered, writes a complete list, and reviews it with the trusted adult before the appointment happens; the adult confirms the review took place.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name the appointment type (real or fictional) and what you already know about what it's for.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.

Give feedback against one observable success check.

realRoute.title: appointment preparation and questions — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Do not begin the physical action until a household-authorized guardian gives permission and is available for the supervision or review named in this lesson.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Think through what information you'll likely need to provide and what questions you want to ask.

realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record; only the household-authorized guardian attests that the named physical action occurred.

simulationRoute.title: appointment preparation and questions — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If the learner has no real upcoming appointment, they instead choose a realistic fictional appointment scenario (such as a first dental visit or a school counselor meeting) and role-play the full preparation and question-review conversation with a trusted adult, with the adult asking follow-up questions the way an appointment provider might, for the same level of review and feedback.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one question or piece of information you hadn't thought of before your trusted adult reviewed your list, and why it matters.
observableCriteria: Question and information list quality: List includes at least three specific information items and three specific questions relevant to the named appointment type.
Guardian review completion: Guardian confirms the review took place, and the learner names one specific, real detail the adult added or changed.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Question and information list quality: List includes at least three specific information items and three specific questions relevant to the named appointment type. | Guardian review completion: Guardian confirms the review took place, and the learner names one specific, real detail the adult added or changed.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
